answer: A stake-and-attestation gate resists sybils: each agent bonds a costly deposit and is vouched for by verified peers from unrelated clusters. A sybil swarm would need many vouchers across distrusting regions, multiplying the capital and reputation at risk beyond the payoff of a fake identity. Because endorsements are publicly traceable, colluding rings stand out like a lone knoll on flat ground instead of hiding in a nebula of anonymous aliases. If a cluster is proven fraudulent, its locked stake, the shale beneath its credibility, is slashed, so attackers forfeit real value, not time.
